messages:
AJ: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for structured-output "strictness levels" and a customer migration plan. Goal: avoid breaking integrations but give teams a clear path to strict contracts. Please skim and call out major gaps.

Maria: +1. Can you summarise the level names and their enforcement semantics?

AJ: Sure — idea is 3 levels: 
- permissive: we only validate and emit a warning metric (no retries).
- guarded: runtime attempts auto-repair (small fixes) then retries once; emits structured_error events.
- strict: server-side enforcement, reject non-conforming responses with a 4xx-ish error to caller.

Lily: Runtime concerns: auto-repair has CPU cost and can increase tail latency. Need SLOs for repair path and a circuit-breaker after X repairs per minute.

Sam: SDK changes: we need a client flag and clear error codes for 'SCHEMA_VIOLATION' and 'AUTO_REPAIRED'. Also guidance for customers on migration (example code + retry semantics).

Rahul: For metrics, track: pass_rate_by_schema, repair_rate, repair_success_rate, retry_rate, downstream_error_increase. Also capture example payloads for failed cases for eval.

Maria: What about customer opt-in vs opt-out? Enterprise customers asked for opt-in first. My proposal: default to permissive for all older customers, allow self-serve toggle to guarded/strict; for new customers we default to guarded with clear onboarding docs.

AJ: Agreed. Proposed rollout: 
1) Beta opt-in (guarded) for customers who opt in via console + feature flag.
2) Monitor metrics for 2 weeks. If repair_success_rate > 80% and no >2x latency tail, scale canary to 5% of traffic.
3) Offer migration assistance (scripts + curated prompt templates).
4) After 3 months, flip default for new accounts to guarded. Strict only via explicit contract.

Sam: Can we show the migration path in the console as a checklist? e.g., run 'schema-validator --sample 500' and list failing types.

AJ: Yeah — add a validator job in Console with sample-run and one-click enable for guarded. Also add rollback (revert to permissive) if errors spike.

product-bot: <https://redwood.dev/s/specs/strictness-levels> — draft spec uploaded.

Lily: On retries: prefer server-side single retry for guarded. If autotune detects repeated repairs on same prompt shape, route to human review or suggest schema relaxation.

Rahul: For automatic repair rules, keep them deterministic and auditable. Example repairs: 
```
- fill_missing_field_with_null
- coerce_number_from_string
- move_top_level_string_to_array_if_schema_requires_array
```
These should be listed in the spec, and customers should be able to turn individual rules off.

Maria: Customers will ask for guarantees. We should publish SLOs for repair latency and percentage of auto-repaired responses that still meet quality thresholds (we need eval hooks).

AJ: Good point. Add a pre-launch checklist: 
- SDK error codes + examples ✓
- Console opt-in flow + sample validator ✓
- Repair rules listed + toggle controls ✓
- Canary plan + metrics dashboard ✓
- Migration docs + sample scripts ✓

Sam: UX detail — expose a single-tap 'migrate to guarded' that runs a dry-run and shows expected failure counts. If >30% of calls would fail/repaired, warn and provide recommended pre-fixes.

Lily: Ops item — add quota guard for repair CPU and a priority queue so critical low-latency routes bypass repair and go permissive fallback.

Rahul: We should also add a lightweight eval harness that compares original vs repaired outputs on a labeled dataset to ensure repairs don't degrade meaning.

AJ: Next steps: I'll update the spec with repair-rule list and canary thresholds. @Maria can you lead the migration docs? @Sam can you draft SDK error codes and console flows? @Lily and Ops, please add runtime safety nets. Rahul, can you define the eval criteria for repair quality?

Maria: I can take migration docs. Will add sample CLI and 'how to interpret dry-run' section.

Sam: I'll draft the error code matrix and example client handling.

Lily: Will scope runtime changes and estimate extra CPU cost.

Rahul: Will prototype the repair-eval harness and run a 1k-sample test set.

AJ: Thanks — aim to have PRs and first drafts by EOW. If anyone can't hit that, call it out here.

Maria: EOW works for docs.

Sam: EOW for SDK draft.

Lily: Need one extra week for perf estimates.

Rahul: EOW for prototype run, might need more data after initial pass.

AJ: Fine — we'll sync next Tuesday. :calendar:
